chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Hadeed, who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) and said: 'Our companions have differed regarding the two Harams (Mecca and Medina); some shorten the prayer and some complete it. I am among those who complete it, based on a narration our companions have transmitted regarding completion. I mentioned Abdullah ibn Jundab that he used to complete it. He said: May God have mercy on Ibn Jundab. Then he said to me: Completion is not valid unless you intend to stay for ten days, and pray the voluntary prayers as much as you wish.'

Ibn Hadeed said: 'And it was my preference that he order me to complete [the prayer], so there is no contradiction between these two narrations and the preceding ones, because the command to shorten is only directed towards one who did not intend to stay for ten days, if he believes that completion is obligatory in them. And we did not say that completion in them is obligatory, but rather we said it is in the manner of excellence and recommendation.'

Do you not see the narration of Ali ibn Hadeed from Al-Reza (peace be upon him) which implies that when Abdullah ibn Jundab was mentioned to him and that he used to complete [the prayer] in them, he had mercy on him? If his command to shorten was in the manner of obligation, he would not have had mercy on him, because he would be opposing him. Then Ali ibn Hadeed also clarified that at the end of the narration, because he said: 'And it was my preference that he order me to complete,' which clarified that he sought obligation, so he did not order him with that, because their commands (peace be upon them) imply obligation, and he did not say 'and he did not recommend it to me.'

And these two narrations can bear another meaning, which is that whoever arrives in the two Harams should intend to stay for ten days and complete the prayer in them, even if he knows that he will not stay except for one day or two days. And this is what distinguishes these two places and sets them apart from other lands, because in other places, if a person does not intend to stay for ten days, it is not permissible for him to complete [the prayer]. And that which reveals this meaning.

key_terms.الإِتمَام: Completing the prayer (praying four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الاستِحبَاب: Recommendation (a legal status between obligation and permissibility)
key_terms.التّقصِير: Shortening the prayer (praying two rak'ahs instead of four)
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيّامٍ: Ten days (the period of stay for completing prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening or completing prayers in Mecca and Medina for visitors?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the Shia juristic resolution regarding the ten-day residency rule (*iqamah*) in Mecca and Medina, distinguishing between the obligatory shortening of prayer for transient visitors and the recommended completion (*tamm*) for those intending a longer stay. Imam Al-Reza’s affirmation of Abdullah ibn Jundab’s practice underscores that completion is a virtue (*fadl*) rather than a strict obligation, thereby harmonizing seemingly contradictory reports by contextualizing the intent of the traveler. This specific ruling for the two Harams serves as a unique exception to the general rule of shortening prayers in other lands, emphasizing the spiritual status of these holy sites.
